The bottleneck on what you can build is no longer *what you already know* — it's your workflow discipline and your ability to direct an agent. This course teaches you to use AI coding agents like [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) and [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) to build ambitious things you don't yet know how to build, while developing the professional engineering habits — version control with Git and GitHub, testing, continuous integration with GitHub Actions, and deployment with GitHub Pages — that make agentic work sustainable and trustworthy. The course runs in two parts. In **Part 1: Working with an agent**, we start with Git by hand, look under the hood at how large language models work (and fail), and then climb from high-touch collaboration with an agent toward delegating work and automatically verifying it. In **Part 2: Building with LLMs**, we apply the workflow to real data analysis in Python (polars, plotnine, and Great Tables), call LLMs from your own code with chatlas, connect agents to tools with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and orchestrate multiple agents. Each week pairs a hands-on workflow concept taught live in class with an ambitious take-home build — a deployed personal website, a novel in an author's voice, a video game, a cloud robot, an AI-powered tool, and more — and a short reading that connects the work to the bigger picture. A team project runs alongside, with in-class studio time for collaboration. By the end, you'll have transferable engineering workflow skills, the ability to work with code and data through an agent, the judgment to know when to trust (and when to verify) AI output, and — most importantly — the ability to teach yourself new domains so you can tackle harder problems in the future.
